title: A formal proof with an intentionally smaller world
summary: The Uniswap V2 audit proved bytecode-level single-call specifications while explicitly excluding the multi-call constant-product invariant and assuming particular token behavior.

case_study.situation: Runtime Verification specified and proved almost every single-call state transition in the built Uniswap V2 contracts. The work was unusually rigorous and operated directly against bytecode.
case_study.turning_point: The report explicitly separated those functional specifications from the contract-level constant-product invariant and limited the proofs to assumed token semantics.
case_study.lesson: Formal verification is only as broad as its specifications and assumptions. The prestige of the method cannot enlarge the world the proof actually describes.

claim: The formal-verification result establishes the fee-adjusted constant-product invariant for arbitrary Uniswap V2 pairs across sequences of calls.
evidence_boundary: The published proofs cover almost all single-call state transitions relative to specifications and assumptions. They do not prove multi-call contract invariants, arbitrary token semantics, sqrt correctness, or all behavior around unknown external calls.

decision.question: May the published formal-verification result be cited as proof of the contract-level x*y=k invariant for an arbitrary token pair?
decision.expected: No. The report expressly excludes that invariant and assumes token behavior; a new claim needs additional specifications and proofs.

missing_edges: A contract-level specification and proof for the fee-adjusted constant-product invariant across calls.
A proof regenerated for token implementations that deviate from the assumed semantics.

recommendations.action: Write and prove a contract-level specification for the cross-call invariant.
recommendations.because: The published single-call specifications explicitly do not establish that property.

recommendations.action: Re-evaluate the proofs for any token outside the assumed semantics.
recommendations.because: The published result is conditional on token behavior matching the stated model.
